prerequisites: Ability to solve algebraic and transcendental equations and inequalities

learning_outcomes.text: Knowledge and understanding of the principles of Mathematical Analysis.
Knowledge of the elements of differential calculus.
Knowledge of the elements of integral calculus.
Conscious use of differential calculus tools.
Conscious use of integral calculus tools.
Ability to formalize and solve problems related to the structural disciplines of the study course.
Ability for critical and reflective analysis in verifying the correctness of an argumentative/demonstrative process and/or a sequence of mathematical calculations.
Using scientific language with ease and mastery.
Ability to find analogies and connections even in contexts and situations not presented during the course.

syllabus_topics: MODULE B (B1) Improper integrals and numerical series
(B3) Real functions of several real variables
(B4) Differential calculus for functions of several real variables

assessment_methods.method: Written exam (Exercise 1: Real and/or complex numbers, real functions)
Written exam (Exercise 2: Limits and differential calculus for functions of one variable)
Written exam (Exercise 3: Integral calculus for functions of one variable)
Written exam (Exercise 4: Theoretical question on Module I topics)
Written exam (Exercise 5: Improper integrals and/or numerical series and/or multiple integrals)
Written exam (Exercise 6: Differential calculus for functions of several variables)
Written exam (Exercise 8: Theoretical question on Module II topics)

assessment_rules: The exam will be predominantly written, lasting 3 hours. Minimum requirements for passing the exam are a basic knowledge of function limits, differential calculus in one and more variables, integral calculus in one and more variables, numerical series, and differential equations. To achieve the minimum grade of 18/30, students must demonstrate basic knowledge of these topics. The final grade, expressed out of thirty, will reflect the student's ability to solve exercises and answer theoretical questions. Maximum evaluation will be given for an exam demonstrating full capability in these areas.
